blocks.text: I can explain how to use representations to calculate unknown values.
In this lesson you will use bar models to solve ratio problems, and find out how many things can change, or vary, in a problem.
Tap the word to see what it means.

items.def: A variable is a value which can be represented by more than one number within a situation or equation.

blocks.text: In ratio problems, the ratio stays true but the values can change. Think about what stays the same and what can change.
Each team in a school quiz is made up of 2 adults and 3 children.
For every 2 adults there are 3 children. For every 3 children there are 2 adults.
How many people are in each quiz team? 2 + 3 = 5 people.

slides.title: Bar models for the quiz team

blocks.text: One way: a single bar with 2 parts for the adults and 3 parts for the children.
Adults [1][1]  Children [1][1][1]
Another way: two bars, one for the adults and one for the children, with the whole team shown along the top.

blocks.label: Where is the whole team?
blocks.text: The whole team is the whole length of the bar: 2 adults and 3 children make 5 people in one quiz team.
If there are 3 teams, there are 3 times as many people, 3 times as many adults and 3 times as many children.

rows.note: People: 5 in one team × 3 teams = 15 people.
Adults: 2 in one team × 3 teams = 6 adults.
Children: 3 in one team × 3 teams = 9 children.

blocks.text: We multiply everything by 3.
This time we change the number of children. There were 3 children in one team and now there are 6, so there are 2 times as many.
To keep the ratio the same we need 2 times as many adults: 2 × 2 = 4 adults.
There are 2 teams, so 5 × 2 = 10 people in all.
Whichever value we change, we multiply all the others by the same amount.
Each team has 2 adults and 3 children.

items.q: There are 4 teams. How many children?
There are 9 children. How many teams?
There are 9 children. How many adults?
There are 20 people in total. How many adults?

blocks.text: Take 3 × 5 = 15 for the quiz teams.

items: **3** is the number of children in one team (3 parts of the bar).
**15** is the number of children when there are 5 teams.

blocks.text: So if there are 5 teams there will be 15 children. Every value in the bar is multiplied by 5.
Each team has 2 adults and 3 children. Decide if each statement is true or false.

items.q: If there are 8 teams, there will be 24 children.
If there are 12 adults, there will be 15 children.
If there are 21 children, there will be 7 teams.

blocks.label: Check the working
blocks.text: 8 teams: 3 × 8 = 24 children, so the first is true. 12 adults is 6 teams (2 × 6 = 12), so there are 3 × 6 = 18 children, not 15, so the second is false. 21 children is 7 teams (3 × 7 = 21), so the third is true.
If a team has 3 children, then however many complete teams you have, the number of children is a multiple of 3.
14 is not a multiple of 3. So 14 children cannot make a whole number of teams.
A variable is a value that can be represented by more than one number within a ratio problem.
In the quiz problem we can vary 3 things:
When we change one of them, that tells us how to change the others.
For every cheese and tomato sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato.
There are 4 variables, because you can vary the number of:
The whole bar is 1 sandwich, and each part of the bar is one ingredient: bread [1][1], cheese [1][1][1], tomato [1][1][1][1].

How many sandwiches can you make with 26 slices of bread? 2 slices for each sandwich, so 26 ÷ 2 = 13 sandwiches. You need 13 times as much cheese and tomato as for 1 sandwich: 13 × 3 = 39 slices of cheese and 13 × 4 = 52 slices of tomato.
How many slices of cheese for 100 sandwiches? 100 times as much cheese: 100 × 3 = 300 slices.
You use 28 slices of tomato. 28 ÷ 4 = 7 sandwiches, so you need 7 times as much cheese: 7 × 3 = 21 slices.
A pack of cheese has 25 slices. How many sandwiches can you make?
Each sandwich uses 3 slices of cheese. 25 is not a multiple of 3, but 24 is a multiple of 3 (3 × 8 = 24).
24 slices make 8 sandwiches, with 1 slice of cheese left over.
Each sandwich uses 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato.

items.q: 30 slices of bread make how many sandwiches?
10 sandwiches need how many slices of tomato?
36 slices of cheese make how many sandwiches?
20 slices of tomato need how many slices of cheese?

blocks.text: Aisha is making pancakes. For every 2 eggs, she uses 3 spoons of sugar and 6 spoons of flour.
All values are the same multiple of the original values. If she uses 4 times as many eggs, she needs 4 times as much sugar and flour: 8 eggs, 12 spoons of sugar and 24 spoons of flour.

items.q: Aisha uses 18 spoons of flour. How many eggs?
Aisha uses 15 spoons of sugar. How many eggs?
Aisha uses 6 eggs. How many spoons of sugar?

slides.title: Explain how to represent ratio and to calculate unknown values

items: You can use a bar model to represent a ratio problem.
A variable is a value that can change within a ratio problem, such as the number of teams, adults and children.
You can use multiplication and division to calculate unknown values.
The bar model helps you see the relationship between the variables in the ratio problem.

flashcards.back: A value which can be represented by more than one number within a situation or equation.

flashcards.front: A quiz team has 2 adults and 3 children. How many people are in one team?
Where is the whole team on a bar model?
flashcards.back: The whole length of the bar.

flashcards.front: Quiz teams have 2 adults and 3 children. There are 3 teams. How many people?
Quiz teams have 2 adults and 3 children. There are 5 teams. How many children?
flashcards.back:
15 children.

Every value is multiplied by 5, so 3 × 5 = 15.

flashcards.front: Why can’t there be 14 children in the quiz teams (3 children per team)?
flashcards.back: 14 is not a multiple of 3, so it does not make a whole number of teams.

flashcards.front: How many variables are there in the cheese and tomato sandwich problem?
flashcards.back: 4: sandwiches, slices of bread, slices of cheese and slices of tomato.

flashcards.front: Sandwich: 2 bread, 3 cheese, 4 tomato. How many sandwiches from 26 slices of bread?
Sandwich: 2 bread, 3 cheese, 4 tomato. How much cheese for 100 sandwiches?
Sandwich: 2 bread, 3 cheese, 4 tomato. You have 25 slices of cheese. How many sandwiches, and what is left?
flashcards.back:
8 sandwiches, with 1 slice of cheese left over.

25 is not a multiple of 3 but 24 is.

flashcards.front: Pancakes: 2 eggs, 3 spoons of sugar, 6 spoons of flour. What do 8 eggs need?
flashcards.back:
12 spoons of sugar and 24 spoons of flour.

All values are multiplied by 4.

flashcards.front: In a ratio problem, if you multiply one value by 2, what do you do to the others?
flashcards.back: Multiply them all by 2 as well, to keep the ratio the same.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Explain how to represent ratio and to calculate unknown values
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a number. Drawing a bar model first can help you.

questions.prompt: Each quiz team has 2 adults and 3 children. There are 6 teams. How many children are there?
questions.explanation: There are 6 times as many children as in one team: 3 × 6 = 18.

questions.prompt: Each quiz team has 2 adults and 3 children. There are 12 adults. How many children are there?
questions.explanation: 12 adults is 6 teams (2 × 6 = 12), so there are 3 × 6 = 18 children.

questions.prompt: Each quiz team has 2 adults and 3 children. How many people are there in 4 teams?
For every cheese and tomato sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato. How many variables are there in this problem?
questions.explanation: You can vary the number of sandwiches, slices of bread, slices of cheese and slices of tomato.

questions.prompt: For every sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato. How many sandwiches can you make from a loaf with 26 slices of bread?
questions.explanation: Each sandwich uses 2 slices of bread and 26 ÷ 2 = 13.

questions.prompt: For every sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato. How many slices of cheese do you need to make 100 sandwiches?
questions.explanation: You need 100 times as much cheese: 100 × 3 = 300.

questions.prompt: For every sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato. You use 28 slices of tomato. How many slices of cheese will you need?
questions.explanation: 28 slices of tomato make 28 ÷ 4 = 7 sandwiches, and 7 × 3 = 21 slices of cheese.

questions.prompt: For every sandwich you need 2 slices of bread, 3 slices of cheese and 4 slices of tomato. A pack of cheese has 25 slices. How many whole sandwiches can you make?
questions.explanation: 25 is not a multiple of 3 but 24 is, and 24 ÷ 3 = 8 sandwiches (1 slice left over).

questions.prompt: For every 2 eggs, Aisha uses 3 spoons of sugar and 6 spoons of flour. She uses 6 eggs. How many spoons of flour does she need?
questions.explanation: 6 eggs is 3 times 2 eggs, so she needs 6 × 3 = 18 spoons of flour.

questions.prompt: For every 2 eggs, Aisha uses 3 spoons of sugar and 6 spoons of flour. She uses 15 spoons of sugar. How many eggs does she need?
questions.explanation: 15 spoons of sugar is 3 × 5, so she needs 2 × 5 = 10 eggs.
